subject: Lighter post-mortem on trader API-key compromise
claim: Lighter attributed the November 16 incident to a trader’s external signing software and said its protocol and infrastructure were unaffected. It restored withdrawals and reported returning roughly $5 million USDC to the trader.

posts.note: Announces an investigation and a precautionary pause to withdrawals and pool creation.
Reports that deposits and withdrawals have resumed.

subject: X League confirms LINE account data exposure via COMSBI
aliases: X League confirms massive data breach
claim: The league reported up to 13,126 exposed LINE account records through its external account-management provider. Smaller subsets contained additional personal details.

posts.note: Reports the LINE account record count and smaller contact-data subset.

subject: Bell Canada reports theft of enterprise customer data
claim: Bell reported theft of enterprise customer data in a November 17 intrusion. The number of affected people or organizations was not disclosed.

claim: Optimizely said a third party modified scripts used by some Web Experimentation customers. It removed the injected code and contacted affected customers.

claim: Proxima said 5,324.2 SOL was stolen across 870 addresses belonging to 181 users after diagnostic logs exposed wallet-key material. It said its treasury covered confirmed losses.

subject: Cursor marketplace served backdoored Claude Code extension after Fireworks AI key exposure
claim: Cursor confirmed tampered copies of the Claude Code extension (2.1.312 and 2.1.313) were served from its marketplace cache for about 11 hours on October 29, reaching at most 5,000 users. Its November 13 update traced the attack to an access key exposed at its vendor Fireworks AI, which led to coding-agent traces with unredacted credentials and then to internal SaaS tools. Uber and Notion have also reported data exposed through Fireworks.
